<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabaseState;
use Symfony\Component\Process\ExecutableFinder;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Tests\Upgrade\LoadsV02Fixture;

uses(LoadsV02Fixture::class);

beforeEach(function (): void {
    if (app(VaulterDatabase::class)->driver() !== 'pgsql' || (new ExecutableFinder)->find('psql') === null) {
        $this->markTestSkipped('Upgrade fixtures require PostgreSQL and psql.');
    }
});

afterEach(function (): void {
    $db = app(VaulterDatabase::class)->connection();
    if ($db->getDriverName() === 'pgsql' && str_ends_with($db->getDatabaseName(), '_test') && $db->transactionLevel() === 0) {
        $db->getSchemaBuilder()->dropAllTables();
    }

    RefreshDatabaseState::$migrated = false;
});

it('preserves historical rows and event subscriptions through upgrade rollback and retry', function (string $strategy): void {
    $this->loadV02Fixture($strategy);
    $db = app(VaulterDatabase::class)->connection();
    $map = ['storage.created' => 'drive.created', 'node.created' => 'folder.created', 'version.created' => 'file.revision_added', 'node.force_deleted' => 'node.purged', 'upload_session.initiated' => 'upload.initiated', 'upload_session.aborted' => 'upload.aborted', 'upload_session.expired' => 'upload.expired'];
    $subscriptions = ['storage.created', 'node.created', 'storage.created', '*', 'third.party'];
    $db->table('v_webhook_endpoints')->update(['events' => json_encode($subscriptions)]);
    $shares = $db->table('v_node_shares')->orderBy('id')->get()->mapWithKeys(fn ($row): array => [$row->id => $row->revoked_at ?? $row->deleted_at]);
    $owners = $db->table('v_storages')->orderBy('id')->pluck('owner_id')->map(fn ($id): string => (string) $id)->all();
    $events = [];
    foreach (['v_activity' => 'verb', 'v_outbox' => 'event', 'v_webhook_deliveries' => 'event'] as $table => $column) {
        $events[$table] = $db->table($table)->orderBy('id')->get(['id', $column])->mapWithKeys(fn ($row): array => [$row->id => $map[$row->$column] ?? $row->$column])->all();
    }

    $this->artisan('migrate', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    foreach (['drives' => 3, 'nodes' => 40, 'files' => 16, 'file_revisions' => 22, 'file_revision_blobs' => 22, 'node_grants' => 3, 'node_shares' => 4, 'activity' => 74, 'outbox' => 68, 'webhook_deliveries' => 4, 'webhook_endpoints' => 1] as $entity => $count) {
        expect($db->table(Config::table($entity))->count())->toBe($count);
    }

    expect($db->table('v_drives')->orderBy('id')->pluck('owner_id')->all())->toBe($owners);
    expect($db->table('v_node_shares')->orderBy('id')->pluck('revoked_at', 'id')->all())->toBe($shares->all());

    $file = $db->table('v_files')->join('v_nodes', 'v_nodes.id', '=', 'v_files.node_id')->where('v_nodes.name', 'q1.csv')->orderBy('v_files.id')->value('v_files.id');
    expect($db->table('v_file_revisions')->where('file_id', $file)->orderBy('number')->pluck('number')->all())->toBe([1, 2, 3])
        ->and($db->table('v_file_revisions')->where('scan_status', '<>', 'not_required')->count())->toBe(0);
    foreach (['v_activity' => 'verb', 'v_outbox' => 'event', 'v_webhook_deliveries' => 'event'] as $table => $column) {
        expect($db->table($table)->whereIn($column, array_keys($map))->count())->toBe(0)
            ->and($db->table($table)->whereIn('id', array_keys($events[$table]))->orderBy('id')->pluck($column, 'id')->all())->toBe($events[$table]);
    }

    expect(json_decode((string) $db->table('v_webhook_endpoints')->value('events'), true))->toBe(array_map(fn (string $event): string => $map[$event] ?? $event, $subscriptions));
    $before = $db->table('migrations')->count();
    $this->artisan('migrate', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    expect($db->table('migrations')->count())->toBe($before);
    // Replaying each new migration also proves step-level guards.
    foreach (['000001_vaulter_preflight', '000002_rename_storages_to_drives', '000004_file_revisions', '000008_grants_shares_cleanup', '000009_events'] as $name) {
        (require __DIR__.'/../../database/migrations/2026_10_01_'.$name.'.php')->up();
    }

    $this->artisan('migrate:rollback', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    expect($db->getSchemaBuilder()->hasTable('v_storages'))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($db->getSchemaBuilder()->hasTable('v_file_versions'))->toBeTrue()
        ->and(json_decode((string) $db->table('v_webhook_endpoints')->value('events'), true))->toBe($subscriptions);
    $this->artisan('migrate', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    expect($db->table('v_drives')->count())->toBe(3)
        ->and($db->table('v_file_revisions')->count())->toBe(22)
        ->and($db->table('v_node_grants')->count())->toBe(3);
})->with(['bigint', 'ulid']);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabaseState;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Tests\Upgrade\LoadsV02Fixture;

uses(LoadsV02Fixture::class);

afterEach(function (): void {
    $db = app(VaulterDatabase::class)->connection();
    if ($db->getDriverName() === 'pgsql' && str_ends_with($db->getDatabaseName(), '_test') && $db->transactionLevel() === 0) {
        $db->getSchemaBuilder()->dropAllTables();
    }

    RefreshDatabaseState::$migrated = false;
});

function vaulterSchemaSnapshot(): array
{
    $db = app(VaulterDatabase::class)->connection();
    $schema = $db->getSchemaBuilder();
    $result = [];
    foreach ($schema->getTableListing() as $table) {
        $table = str_replace('public.', '', $table);
        if (!str_starts_with($table, 'v_')) {
            continue;
        }

        foreach ($schema->getColumns($table) as $column) {
            unset($column['comment']);
            $result[$table]['columns'][$column['name']] = $column;
        }

        foreach ($schema->getIndexes($table) as $index) {
            $result[$table]['indexes'][$index['name']] = $index;
        }

        foreach ($schema->getForeignKeys($table) as $key) {
            $result[$table]['foreign_keys'][$key['name']] = $key;
        }

        // Includes expressions and partial predicates omitted by getIndexes().
        foreach ($db->select('select indexname, indexdef from pg_indexes where schemaname = ? and tablename = ?', ['public', $table]) as $index) {
            $result[$table]['index_sql'][$index->indexname] = $index->indexdef;
        }

        foreach ($result[$table] as &$part) {
            ksort($part);
        }

        unset($part);
    }

    ksort($result);

    return $result;
}

function vaulterSchemaDifferences(array $upgrade, array $fresh): array
{
    $differences = [];
    foreach (array_unique([...array_keys($upgrade), ...array_keys($fresh)]) as $table) {
        foreach (array_unique([...array_keys($upgrade[$table] ?? []), ...array_keys($fresh[$table] ?? [])]) as $part) {
            foreach (array_unique([...array_keys($upgrade[$table][$part] ?? []), ...array_keys($fresh[$table][$part] ?? [])]) as $name) {
                $before = $upgrade[$table][$part][$name] ?? null;
                $after = $fresh[$table][$part][$name] ?? null;
                if ($before !== $after) {
                    $differences[sprintf('%s.%s.%s', $table, $part, $name)] = ['upgrade' => $before, 'fresh' => $after];
                }
            }
        }
    }

    ksort($differences);

    return $differences;
}

it('matches the fresh schema after upgrading each historical strategy', function (string $strategy): void {
    if (app(VaulterDatabase::class)->driver() !== 'pgsql') {
        $this->markTestSkipped('Schema parity requires PostgreSQL.');
    }

    $this->loadV02Fixture($strategy);
    $this->artisan('migrate', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    $upgrade = vaulterSchemaSnapshot();
    config()->set('vaulter.features.document_versions', true);
    config()->set('vaulter.features.comments', true);
    $this->artisan('migrate:fresh', ['--force' => true])->assertSuccessful();
    $differences = vaulterSchemaDifferences($upgrade, vaulterSchemaSnapshot());
    $path = dirname(__DIR__, 4).'/plans/2026.09.29-№1-VAULTER-STABLE/artifacts/P2.7';
    if (getenv('VAULTER_CAPTURE_PARITY_BASELINE') === '1') {
        file_put_contents(sprintf('%s/parity-baseline-%s.json', $path, $strategy), json_encode($differences, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES)."\n");
        expect(true)->toBeTrue();

        return;
    }

    expect($differences)->toBe([]);
})->with(['bigint', 'ulid']);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * F-P4.1-01 / F-P4.1-02 (VLT-REMED P4.3, batch B16) — schema green guard, no
 * behaviour delta (D19): the hot-path index shape SchemaBuilder emits (and
 * the 2026_07_11_000001 upgrade migration repairs on a pre-fix database) must
 * carry the (trashed_at) scan index PurgeTrashCommand's predicate needs, and
 * must NOT carry the three indexes whose column set duplicates/prefixes another
 * index already on the same table (findings/P4.1-query-indexes.md §0/C7).
 *
 * Red-before (F-P4.1-01): before this item, `v_nodes` carried no index with
 * `columns === ['trashed_at']` — the first assertion below failed. Red-before
 * (F-P4.1-02): before this item, `v_nodes` carried `['drive_id','parent_id']`
 * as its OWN index (inline, alongside the composite), `v_blobs` carried
 * `['status']` as its own index (inline, alongside `_gc_idx`), and `v_activity`
 * carried TWO indexes with `columns === ['created_at']` (the inline one and
 * `_created_idx`) — the negative/count assertions below failed.
 */
function hotPathIndexColumnSets(string $table): array
{
    /** @var list<array{name: string, columns: list<string>}> $indexes */
    $indexes = Schema::getIndexes($table);

    return array_map(static fn (array $index): array => $index['columns'], $indexes);
}

it('v_nodes carries a (trashed_at) scan index for the purge-trash predicate (F-P4.1-01)', function (): void {
    expect(hotPathIndexColumnSets('v_nodes'))->toContain(['trashed_at']);
});

it('v_nodes does not carry a redundant (drive_id, parent_id) index — a strict prefix of (drive_id, parent_id, position) (F-P4.1-02)', function (): void {
    $columnSets = hotPathIndexColumnSets('v_nodes');

    expect($columnSets)->not->toContain(['drive_id', 'parent_id'])
        ->and($columnSets)->toContain(['drive_id', 'parent_id', 'position']);
});

it('v_blobs does not carry a redundant single-column status index — a strict prefix of the GC index (F-P4.1-02)', function (): void {
    $columnSets = hotPathIndexColumnSets('v_blobs');

    expect($columnSets)->not->toContain(['status'])
        ->and($columnSets)->toContain(['status', 'ref_count', 'delete_after_at']);
})->skip(fn (): bool => !Config::featureEnabled('blobs'), 'v_blobs only exists when the blobs feature is enabled');

it('v_activity carries the (created_at) feed index exactly once, not twice (F-P4.1-02)', function (): void {
    $duplicates = array_filter(
        hotPathIndexColumnSets('v_activity'),
        static fn (array $columns): bool => $columns === ['created_at'],
    );

    expect($duplicates)->toHaveCount(1);
})->skip(fn (): bool => !Config::featureEnabled('activity'), 'v_activity only exists when the activity feature is enabled');

/**
 * The read shape of a storage container (§2.1): its meta, the root node the
 * client opens into, and the used/quota accounting the UI shows as a usage bar.
 * Read-only — it transforms an already-loaded Storage, never WRITES (it resolves the
 * root node through the read repository, never the provisioning StorageManager).
 *
 * @mixin Drive
 */
final class StorageResource extends JsonResource
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    #[\Override]
    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        /** @var Drive $storage */
        $storage = $this->resource;

        return [
            'id' => $storage->getKey(),
            'panel' => $storage->profile,
            'owner' => [
                'type' => $storage->owner_type,
                'id' => $storage->owner_id,
            ],
            'name' => $storage->name,
            'slug' => null,
            'root_node_id' => $storage->root_node_id,
            'disk' => $storage->disk,
            'storage_type' => null,
            'used_bytes' => $storage->used_bytes,
            'quota_bytes' => $storage->quota_bytes,
            'status' => $storage->status,
            'created_at' => $storage->created_at,
            'updated_at' => $storage->updated_at,
            // What the request actor may do on the storage ROOT (§2.6 / H.2),
            // resolved through the AccessResolver so the Vue client gates its
            // toolbar (open the storage, create folders, upload, manage).
            'abilities' => $this->abilities($request, $storage),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * The storage-root ability flags the Vue toolbar binds against, resolved through
     * the AccessResolver for the request's actor (§2.6 / H.2). Mapped to the four
     * frontend keys: view (View on root), create_folder + upload (Create on root,
     * AND the workspace-create gate), manage (Manage on root).
     *
     * Resilience: with no acting user OR no provisioned root node yet, every flag is
     * false — a read-only shell (the SAFE default; the toolbar advertises nothing it
     * cannot back). The Resource never WRITES, so a missing root is resolved as
     * "nothing yet", never auto-provisioned here.
     *
     * @return array<string, bool>
     */
    private function abilities(Request $request, Drive $storage): array
    {
        $actor = $this->actor($request);
        $root = $this->root($storage);

        if ($actor === null || !$root instanceof Node) {
            return [
                'view' => false,
                'create_folder' => false,
                'upload' => false,
                'manage' => false,
            ];
        }

        $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);
        $flags = $resolver->abilitiesFor($actor, $root);

        $canCreate = ($flags[Ability::Create->value] ?? false)
            && $resolver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $storage);

        return [
            'view' => $flags[Ability::View->value] ?? false,
            'create_folder' => $canCreate,
            'upload' => $canCreate,
            'manage' => $flags[Ability::Manage->value] ?? false,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * The storage root node, resolved READ-ONLY through the read repository (never the
     * provisioning StorageManager — a Resource must not write). Null when the storage
     * has no root_node_id yet, or the row is missing.
     */
    private function root(Drive $storage): ?Node
    {
        if ($storage->root_node_id === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return app(NodeReadRepository::class)->find($storage->root_node_id);
    }

    /**
     * The acting authorizable for the request, or null when unauthenticated.
     */
    private function actor(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}

1→# Upgrade Guide

This file documents breaking changes and how to migrate through them. Entries are ordered
newest-first. See `CHANGELOG.md` for the full list of changes per release; this file only covers
changes that require action from consumers of the package.

## Unreleased

### Canonical schema 0.3 (P2.7)
10→
Back up the database and object store before running `php artisan migrate --force`
in production. Stop application writes during the code/schema upgrade; deploy the
canonical code and migrate stored events together. Migration №1 refuses soft-deleted
nodes, drives or files, documents without revisions, and own-tables installations.
It lists offending rows/tables and recommends `vaulter:upgrade:inspect` (planned for
P7; it is not shipped yet). Resolve these conditions before retrying.

The existing base migration filenames stay unchanged. Fresh installs create all
core tables regardless of feature flags; those flags still control runtime behavior.
20→The upgrade sequence includes the existing №3 host keys, №6 second-root repair and
№7 blob scopes between these new steps:

| Migration | Change |
|---|---|
| №1 `2026_10_01_000001_vaulter_preflight` | Read-only safety checks before any rename. |
| №2 `…000002_rename_storages_to_drives` | Normalize legacy table overrides, rename `storages` to `drives`, `panel` to `profile` and `storage_id` to `drive_id`; create missing core tables. |
| №4 `…000004_file_revisions` | `file_versions` / `file_version_blobs` become `file_revisions` / `file_revision_blobs`; `version_no` → `number`, `content_sha256` → `sha256`, `file_version_id` → `file_revision_id`. File handles use `current_revision_id` / `revision_count`. Upload sessions use `target_node_id` and nullable result references. |
| №8 `…000008_grants_shares_cleanup` | Hard-delete soft-deleted grants; preserve share revocation as `COALESCE(revoked_at, deleted_at)`; remove deleted/inherited columns and use an ordinary grant UNIQUE. |
| №9 `…000009_events` | Convert activity/outbox/delivery events and endpoint subscription lists; add activity occurrence ID and nullable outbox aggregate columns. |
30→
`Config::table()` now always returns prefix + canonical entity name. Old
`vaulter.table_names` is read only by `Config::legacyTable()` during upgrade.
Drive/File/NodeGrant/NodeShare models no longer use Eloquent `SoftDeletes`.
`Profile::storageType()` and `storageTypeKey()` are removed. HTTP JSON keys such as
`storage_id`, `version_no`, `content_sha256` and `panel` stay unchanged until P6.1;
removed drive metadata `slug` and `storage_type` return null.

Rollback restores historical names, structure and event values, but cannot recover
hard-deleted grants, deleted drive metadata (`slug`, `storage_type`,
40→`default_node_permissions`), or the original grant inheritance fields. Reintroduced
columns use defaults (`storage_type=private`, permissions=31, inherited=false,
nullable fields=null). Share revocation and №6 tree repairs remain in effect. Tables
created for previously disabled features remain. Roll back the full upgrade batch to
reach migration №2: `--step=5` only reaches №4 when all eight upgrade migrations run.
Fresh-install rollback leaves canonical names for the base migrations to drop.

Webhook consumers must update these event names. Subscription conversion preserves
order, duplicates, wildcards and third-party names:

50→| 0.2 | 0.3 |
|---|---|
| `storage.created` | `drive.created` |
| `node.created` | `folder.created` |
| `version.created` | `file.revision_added` |
| `node.force_deleted` | `node.purged` |
| `upload_session.initiated/aborted/expired` | `upload.initiated/aborted/expired` |

Node document versions and the node's `current_version_id`, `file_id`, `deleted_at`
remain until P4.1. Historical PostgreSQL bigint and ULID fixtures are supported;
60→MySQL fresh installation still has the known generated-column/FK blocker owned by
P8.1 (see [database compatibility](docs/guide/database-compatibility.md)).


### Prepared CAS commit and atomic quota (AD21)

Custom implementations of `Vaulter\Contracts\Cas\BlobStore` must add
`commitStaged(StagedObject $staged, BlobScope $scope, ?string $disk = null): Blob`.
It commits prepared bytes without discarding the staged object. Keep `commit()`
as stage → commitStaged → discard in `finally`. The outer upload owns cleanup
70→and reuses prepared bytes on transaction retries.

Quota reservations now run before CAS promotion. Subtree copies that exceed quota
throw the existing `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\QuotaExceededException` and roll
back completely. The core repository throws its common base,
`Vaulter\Exceptions\Drive\QuotaExceededException`; Drive Actions preserve the
existing exception type and HTTP 413 `quota_exceeded` response.


### Lossless CAS scope and migration №7 (AD20)
80→
Replace `BlobStore::commit($stream, tenantId: ..., storageId: ...)` with
`commit($stream, BlobScope::forUpload($dedupScope, $tenantId, (string) $storageId), $disk)`.
`ContentStore::keyFor()` now receives `Vaulter\ValueObjects\Cas\BlobScope`.
Host tenant IDs and drive IDs remain strings without numeric coercion. Tenant scope
with no tenant uses `BlobScope::global()`. Scope IDs contain 1–96 bytes; IDs outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` are encoded as unpadded base64url in physical paths.

Migration `2026_10_01_000007_blob_scope_key` backfills the NOT NULL `scope_key`
and replaces the dedup index with `UNIQUE(scope_key, sha256)`. It preserves all
90→existing `storage_key` values and objects. A uniqueness conflict stops migration
before the old index is removed; investigate the conflicting rows before retrying.
Custom blob schemas must also provide `scope_key`.

After the SQL migrations, inspect and repair mixed legacy areas:

```bash
php artisan vaulter:blobs:repair-scopes --dry-run
php artisan vaulter:blobs:repair-scopes --execute
```
100→
Exactly one mode is required. Review `hash_mismatch` and `unreferenced` reports;
these blobs remain unchanged. Each target commits independently, so a failed copy
can be retried. Old objects stay until GC; successful moves are journalled in
`storage/logs/vaulter-repair-scopes.log`. Target scope comes from revision → file →
node → storage; no tenant is guessed. A storage with NULL tenant belongs to the
host-wide global scope. Reads always use the disk and path recorded on the blob.
Run with operational access to all storages in the affected panel, and pause other
operators changing tenant assignments during repair.

110→The migration's `down()` restores the historical structure using the current
`dedup.scope`; it does not undo object copies or redirected edges. If repaired
rows conflict with the old index, rollback fails before removing `scope_key`.
Take a backup before upgrading or repairing data.

### Exact listing and shared cursors (AD12)

Before: children, search, trash and Filament exposed grant-reachable candidates,
including denied nodes; `shared` used `page`, `current_page` and `total`.
After: all these surfaces and folder `show` children apply effective `View` for every
120→driver. REST listings return `meta.next_cursor`, `per_page`, `scanned`, `path` and a
null `prev_cursor`; `total` and numbered page links are omitted. Replace shared
page-number iteration with `cursor` iteration, and continue through empty pages
while `next_cursor` is non-null. `vaulter.listing.scan_budget` defaults to 1000;
raise it to inspect more candidates per request. Invalid or cross-query cursors
return 422 `validation_failed` with `errors.cursor`.

New PHP surface: `AccessResolver::evaluateMany()`, `AclFolder`, `NodePage` and
`ExactListing`. Listing resource abilities use the batch grant sets.

130→### Tree invariants, second-root repair and migration №6 (AD13)

Before: Actions accepted any node of the drive as a parent, so a folder, upload, move,
copy or document could land inside a file, a document or a trashed folder; a `null`
parent in `CreateDocumentNodeAction` (and in Drive Actions called directly) wrote a
second parentless node that the root listing never showed; the root could be renamed,
moved or trashed; two concurrent moves could form a cycle; `forceDelete` purged live
nodes; restoring or trashing twice was a silent no-op. After:

- A parent or destination must be a live folder of the same drive, checked under row
140→  locks inside the transaction: otherwise `InvalidDestinationException`
  (409, `invalid_destination`); a folder of another drive raises
  `CrossStorageMoveException` (409, `cross_drive_operation`) from Drive Actions and
  `InvalidDestinationException` from `CreateDocumentNodeAction`.
- A `null` destination always means the drive root (`root_node_id`).
- The root cannot be renamed, moved, copied, trashed or force-deleted (409, `invalid_destination`).
- Trashing a node already in the trash raises `InvalidDestinationException`; restoring or
  force-deleting a node that is not in the trash raises `NodeNotTrashedException`
  (409, `node_not_trashed`). Delete a live node by trashing it first.
- Every tree write takes the drive tree lock as its first statement: moves, restores, trashes
150→  and force deletes exclusively (`VaulterDatabase::lockTree()`), creates, uploads, copies and
  renames shared (`VaulterDatabase::lockTreeShared()`, new). Concurrent moves can no longer form a
  cycle (`CycleException`, 409, `node_move_cycle`) and a create cannot slip under a folder being
  trashed. On PostgreSQL the shared lock keeps uploads concurrent with each other but a structural
  operation waits for in-flight uploads of its drive; on MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite the lock is the
  storage row and tree writes of one drive run one at a time. Custom Actions that change the
  tree should take the same locks before locking node rows.
- Names written by create, upload, rename, copy (explicit name) and document creation are
  trimmed, NFC-normalized when ext-intl is installed, and rejected with
  `InvalidNodeNameException` (422, `validation_failed`, `errors.name`) when empty, `.`/`..`,
160→  longer than `vaulter.drive.name_rules.max_length` UTF-8 bytes, or containing `/`, `\`
  or a control character.

Run `php artisan migrate --force` after a database backup. Migration
`2026_10_01_000006_nodes_cleanup` moves every parentless node other than a drive's
`root_node_id` under that root, renaming it `"<base> (legacy N)<.ext>"` when a live root
child already owns the name, writes a `node.moved` activity row (`actor_type`
`vaulter:system`, `context.reason` `n04_repair`, `context.renamed_from`) per move, and then
adds the unique one-root-per-drive index (`{nodes}_root_uniq`; a generated `root_storage`
column on MySQL/MariaDB). It stops without changes when a drive has several parentless
170→nodes and no `root_node_id`: set the real root first. The repair is irreversible —
rollback only drops the index. Re-running the migration changes nothing.

### Independent host keys and migration №3 (AD25)

Before: host owner, subject, author, tenant and actor columns inherited Vaulter's
entity-ID strategy (`char(26)` for ULID or bigint). After: all 27 columns use
`vaulter.ids.host_keys`, default `string` (`varchar(64)`), so UUID users and bigint
projects/roles can coexist with ULID Vaulter IDs. `VaulterSchema::hostKey()` is new;
`actor()` and `tenant()` use the host setting. Entity keys and references keep their strategy.
180→
Run `php artisan migrate --force` in a maintenance window after a database backup.
Migration `2026_10_01_000003_host_key_columns` preserves existing values, column
nullability and indexes, uses `vaulter.connection` and legacy table names, and is

10→
Back up the database and object store before running `php artisan migrate --force`
in production. Stop application writes during the code/schema upgrade; deploy the
canonical code and migrate stored events together. Migration №1 refuses soft-deleted
nodes, drives or files, documents without revisions, and own-tables installations.
It lists offending rows/tables and recommends `vaulter:upgrade:inspect` (planned for
P7; it is not shipped yet). Resolve these conditions before retrying.

The existing base migration filenames stay unchanged. Fresh installs create all
core tables regardless of feature flags; those flags still control runtime behavior.

№7 blob scopes between these new steps:

|---|---|
| №1 `2026_10_01_000001_vaulter_preflight` | Read-only safety checks before any rename. |

60→MySQL fresh installation still has the known generated-column/FK blocker owned by
P8.1 (see [database compatibility](docs/guide/database-compatibility.md)).

as stage → commitStaged → discard in `finally`. The outer upload owns cleanup
70→and reuses prepared bytes on transaction retries.

throw the existing `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\QuotaExceededException` and roll

140→  locks inside the transaction: otherwise `InvalidDestinationException`

`storage_id`, `version_no`, `content_sha256` and `panel` stay unchanged until P6.1;
removed drive metadata `slug` and `storage_type` return null.

Rollback restores historical names, structure and event values, but cannot recover
hard-deleted grants, deleted drive metadata (`slug`, `storage_type`,
`default_node_permissions`), or the original grant inheritance fields. Reintroduced
columns use defaults (`storage_type=private`, permissions=31, inherited=false,
nullable fields=null). Share revocation and №6 tree repairs remain in effect. Tables
created for previously disabled features remain. Roll back the full upgrade batch to
reach migration №2: `--step=5` only reaches №4 when all eight upgrade migrations run.
Fresh-install rollback leaves canonical names for the base migrations to drop.

Webhook consumers must update these event names. Subscription conversion preserves
order, duplicates, wildcards and third-party names:

| 0.2 | 0.3 |
|---|---|
| `storage.created` | `drive.created` |
| `node.created` | `folder.created` |
| `version.created` | `file.revision_added` |
| `node.force_deleted` | `node.purged` |
| `upload_session.initiated/aborted/expired` | `upload.initiated/aborted/expired` |

Node document versions and the node's `current_version_id`, `file_id`, `deleted_at`
remain until P4.1. Historical PostgreSQL bigint and ULID fixtures are supported;
MySQL fresh installation still has the known generated-column/FK blocker owned by
P8.1 (see [database compatibility](docs/guide/database-compatibility.md)).


### Prepared CAS commit and atomic quota (AD21)

Custom implementations of `Vaulter\Contracts\Cas\BlobStore` must add
`commitStaged(StagedObject $staged, BlobScope $scope, ?string $disk = null): Blob`.
It commits prepared bytes without discarding the staged object. Keep `commit()`
as stage → commitStaged → discard in `finally`. The outer upload owns cleanup
and reuses prepared bytes on transaction retries.

Quota reservations now run before CAS promotion. Subtree copies that exceed quota
throw the existing `Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\QuotaExceededException` and roll
back completely. The core repository throws its common base,
`Vaulter\Exceptions\Drive\QuotaExceededException`; Drive Actions preserve the
existing exception type and HTTP 413 `quota_exceeded` response.


### Lossless CAS scope and migration №7 (AD20)

Replace `BlobStore::commit($stream, tenantId: ..., storageId: ...)` with
`commit($stream, BlobScope::forUpload($dedupScope, $tenantId, (string) $storageId), $disk)`.
`ContentStore::keyFor()` now receives `Vaulter\ValueObjects\Cas\BlobScope`.
Host tenant IDs and drive IDs remain strings without numeric coercion. Tenant scope
with no tenant uses `BlobScope::global()`. Scope IDs contain 1–96 bytes; IDs outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` are encoded as unpadded base64url in physical paths.

Migration `2026_10_01_000007_blob_scope_key` backfills the NOT NULL `scope_key`
and replaces the dedup index with `UNIQUE(scope_key, sha256)`. It preserves all
existing `storage_key` values and objects. A uniqueness conflict stops migration
before the old index is removed; investigate the conflicting rows before retrying.
Custom blob schemas must also provide `scope_key`.

After the SQL migrations, inspect and repair mixed legacy areas:

```bash
php artisan vaulter:blobs:repair-scopes --dry-run
php artisan vaulter:blobs:repair-scopes --execute
```

Exactly one mode is required. Review `hash_mismatch` and `unreferenced` reports;
these blobs remain unchanged. Each target commits independently, so a failed copy
can be retried. Old objects stay until GC; successful moves are journalled in
`storage/logs/vaulter-repair-scopes.log`. Target scope comes from revision → file →
node → storage; no tenant is guessed. A storage with NULL tenant belongs to the
host-wide global scope. Reads always use the disk and path recorded on the blob.
Run with operational access to all storages in the affected panel, and pause other
operators changing tenant assignments during repair.

The migration's `down()` restores the historical structure using the current
`dedup.scope`; it does not undo object copies or redirected edges. If repaired
rows conflict with the old index, rollback fails before removing `scope_key`.
Take a backup before upgrading or repairing data.

### Exact listing and shared cursors (AD12)

Before: children, search, trash and Filament exposed grant-reachable candidates,
including denied nodes; `shared` used `page`, `current_page` and `total`.
After: all these surfaces and folder `show` children apply effective `View` for every
driver. REST listings return `meta.next_cursor`, `per_page`, `scanned`, `path` and a
null `prev_cursor`; `total` and numbered page links are omitted. Replace shared
page-number iteration with `cursor` iteration, and continue through empty pages
while `next_cursor` is non-null. `vaulter.listing.scan_budget` defaults to 1000;
raise it to inspect more candidates per request. Invalid or cross-query cursors
return 422 `validation_failed` with `errors.cursor`.

New PHP surface: `AccessResolver::evaluateMany()`, `AclFolder`, `NodePage` and
`ExactListing`. Listing resource abilities use the batch grant sets.

### Tree invariants, second-root repair and migration №6 (AD13)

Before: Actions accepted any node of the drive as a parent, so a folder, upload, move,
copy or document could land inside a file, a document or a trashed folder; a `null`
parent in `CreateDocumentNodeAction` (and in Drive Actions called directly) wrote a
second parentless node that the root listing never showed; the root could be renamed,
moved or trashed; two concurrent moves could form a cycle; `forceDelete` purged live
nodes; restoring or trashing twice was a silent no-op. After:

- A parent or destination must be a live folder of the same drive, checked under row
  locks inside the transaction: otherwise `InvalidDestinationException`
  (409, `invalid_destination`); a folder of another drive raises
  `CrossStorageMoveException` (409, `cross_drive_operation`) from Drive Actions and
  `InvalidDestinationException` from `CreateDocumentNodeAction`.
- A `null` destination always means the drive root (`root_node_id`).
- The root cannot be renamed, moved, copied, trashed or force-deleted (409, `invalid_destination`).
- Trashing a node already in the trash raises `InvalidDestinationException`; restoring or
  force-deleting a node that is not in the trash raises `NodeNotTrashedException`
  (409, `node_not_trashed`). Delete a live node by trashing it first.
- Every tree write takes the drive tree lock as its first statement: moves, restores, trashes
  and force deletes exclusively (`VaulterDatabase::lockTree()`), creates, uploads, copies and
  renames shared (`VaulterDatabase::lockTreeShared()`, new). Concurrent moves can no longer form a
  cycle (`CycleException`, 409, `node_move_cycle`) and a create cannot slip under a folder being
  trashed. On PostgreSQL the shared lock keeps uploads concurrent with each other but a structural
  operation waits for in-flight uploads of its drive; on MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite the lock is the
  storage row and tree writes of one drive run one at a time. Custom Actions that change the
  tree should take the same locks before locking node rows.
- Names written by create, upload, rename, copy (explicit name) and document creation are
  trimmed, NFC-normalized when ext-intl is installed, and rejected with
  `InvalidNodeNameException` (422, `validation_failed`, `errors.name`) when empty, `.`/`..`,
  longer than `vaulter.drive.name_rules.max_length` UTF-8 bytes, or containing `/`, `\`
  or a control character.

Run `php artisan migrate --force` after a database backup. Migration
`2026_10_01_000006_nodes_cleanup` moves every parentless node other than a drive's
`root_node_id` under that root, renaming it `"<base> (legacy N)<.ext>"` when a live root
child already owns the name, writes a `node.moved` activity row (`actor_type`
`vaulter:system`, `context.reason` `n04_repair`, `context.renamed_from`) per move, and then
adds the unique one-root-per-drive index (`{nodes}_root_uniq`; a generated `root_storage`
column on MySQL/MariaDB). It stops without changes when a drive has several parentless
nodes and no `root_node_id`: set the real root first. The repair is irreversible —
rollback only drops the index. Re-running the migration changes nothing.

### Independent host keys and migration №3 (AD25)

Before: host owner, subject, author, tenant and actor columns inherited Vaulter's
entity-ID strategy (`char(26)` for ULID or bigint). After: all 27 columns use
`vaulter.ids.host_keys`, default `string` (`varchar(64)`), so UUID users and bigint
projects/roles can coexist with ULID Vaulter IDs. `VaulterSchema::hostKey()` is new;
`actor()` and `tenant()` use the host setting. Entity keys and references keep their strategy.

Run `php artisan migrate --force` in a maintenance window after a database backup.
Migration `2026_10_01_000003_host_key_columns` preserves existing values, column
nullability and indexes, uses `vaulter.connection` and legacy table names, and is
idempotent. PostgreSQL casts values with `USING`; MySQL/MariaDB modifies column types;
SQLite requires no type upgrade. The migration does not rename the tenant column.

Set `VAULTER_HOST_KEYS` to `bigint`, `uuid` or `ulid` only when every existing host
key fits that type. Incompatible data raises the database driver's error. Rollback
restores the current Vaulter ID strategy; host keys inserted after upgrading (for
example UUIDs into an old ULID installation) can prevent rollback. Do not assume a
structural rollback can accept every new host key.

### Runtime Drive dependencies (AD02)

Documents and Filament now declare `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive` in `require`
rather than `require-dev`; installing either also installs Drive and its Media
backend. Update your Composer lock accordingly. Filament Move now requires
workspace creation access and Create on the destination, including the storage
root. A denied move leaves the node in place and shows "Move not allowed".

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Webhooks\SigningSecretEncryptor;

/**
 * Encrypt the webhook signing_secret at rest (F-P1.7-02). Two idempotent steps:
 *   1. widen the column to text (the ciphertext is longer than the 64-char plaintext);
 *   2. encrypt any existing plaintext secret in place — a value that already decrypts
 *      is left untouched, so re-running is a no-op.
 *
 * Fresh installs already get a text column (SchemaBuilder) and have no plaintext
 * rows, so both steps are no-ops there; the migration exists for a deployment that ran
 * the original string version. Gated on the 'reliability' feature.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        if (!Config::featureEnabled('reliability')) {
            return;
        }

        $table = Config::table('webhook_endpoints');

        if (!Schema::hasTable($table)) {
            return;
        }

        if (Schema::getColumnType($table, 'signing_secret') !== 'text') {
            Schema::table($table, static function (Blueprint $blueprint): void {
                $blueprint->text('signing_secret')->change();
            });
        }

        app(SigningSecretEncryptor::class)->encryptPlaintext($table);
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        if (!Config::featureEnabled('reliability')) {
            return;
        }

        $table = Config::table('webhook_endpoints');

        if (!Schema::hasTable($table)) {
            return;
        }

        app(SigningSecretEncryptor::class)->decryptToPlaintext($table);

        Schema::table($table, static function (Blueprint $blueprint): void {
            $blueprint->string('signing_secret')->change();
        });

title: Drive Profiles
description: Named drive policies over one shared Vaulter schema.
outline: deep
---

# Drive Profiles

A `Vaulter\Profiles\Profile` names a drive policy for a host entity. Profiles share
10→one schema; the `panel` discriminator and the existing `vaulter.panels` / `default_panel`
configuration keys remain unchanged until the configuration/schema transition.
`Vaulter::for($owner, 'project')` opens the drive for that owner and profile.

## Configure a provider

```php
namespace App\Vaulter\Profiles;

use App\Models\Project;
20→use Vaulter\Profiles\Profile;
use Vaulter\Profiles\ProfileProvider;

final class ProjectProfile extends ProfileProvider
{
    public function profile(Profile $profile): Profile
    {
        return $profile->id('project')->host(Project::class)->storageType('team')
            ->withoutGrants()->feature('share_links', true);
    }
30→}
```

Register the FQCN in `config/vaulter.php`:

```php
'panels' => [App\Vaulter\Profiles\ProjectProfile::class],
```

Profiles are hydrated during application boot. The default profile is registered
40→first, so a provider using the same ID can override it. Unknown IDs throw
`Vaulter\Exceptions\Profiles\UnknownProfileException`.

## Registry

```php
$profile = Vaulter::profiles()->get('project');
Vaulter::profiles()->registerProvider(new ProjectProfile);
Vaulter::profiles()->register((new Profile)->id('reports'));
$profiles = Vaulter::profiles()->all();
50→```

The registry exposes `register`, `registerProvider`, `fromConfig`, `get`, `has`, `all`,
and `default`. `Vaulter::panel()/panels()/registerPanel()` have been replaced by this registry.

## Profile builder

| Method | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `id(string)` / `getId()` | Named profile ID |
60→| `host(string)` / `hostModel()` | Host model FQCN |
| `grants()` / `withoutGrants()` / `hasGrants()` | Grants policy |
| `storageType(string)` / `storageTypeKey()` | Current storage policy preset |
| `features(array)` / `feature(string, bool)` / `featureEnabled(string)` | Profile feature settings |

Own-tables settings, per-profile ID strategies, model maps, pipelines and resource hooks
are removed. Profiles do not define separate table names or generate migrations.
`booted()` previously ran after provider registration and is now removed; move any
host initialization to your Laravel service provider. Runtime enforcement of all
profile policies is delivered separately; declaring a feature here does not promise
70→that every existing operation already enforces it.

## Scaffold a provider

```bash
php artisan vaulter:make:profile project --host="App\Models\Project" --no-grants
```

This writes `app/Vaulter/Profiles/ProjectProfile.php` without modifying config or migrations.
Use `--force` to overwrite an existing provider. Own-tables `--prefix/--id` options and
80→`vaulter:panel:migrations` are removed. See UPGRADE.md for the complete breaking API map.

title: Configuration
description: A section-by-section walkthrough of config/vaulter.php — models, table names, id strategy, panels, features, permission drivers, CAS, sharing, uploads, webhooks and collaboration.
outline: deep
---

# Configuration

Publish the config with:
10→
```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=vaulter-config
```

It lands at `config/vaulter.php`. This page walks every section. The config is **cache-safe**
— every swappable binding is a fully-qualified class name (FQCN) string, never a closure — so
`php artisan config:cache` works.

::: tip Looking for a single key?
20→This page is the narrative walkthrough. For an exhaustive, alphabetical lookup table see the
[config-key reference](/reference/configuration).
:::

## Models

Every Vaulter entity is resolved through this map, so you can point any of them at your own
subclass (to add ULID keys, tenant scoping, audit behaviour, …):

```php
30→'models' => [
    // Vaulter Drive entities
    'storage'    => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive::class,
    'node'       => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node::class,
    'file'       => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\File::class,
    'blob'       => \Vaulter\Models\Cas\Blob::class,
    'grant'      => \Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant::class,
    'node_share' => \Vaulter\Models\Sharing\NodeShare::class,
    // …and file_version, file_version_blob, activity, outbox, webhook_endpoint,
    //    webhook_delivery
40→],
```

::: info Drive/Documents-owned models
`upload_session` / `upload_part` are owned by `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`; the
node-attached `node_comment` / `node_document_version` models are owned by
`axioma-studio/vaulter-documents`. Neither ships a default here — each package merges
its own entry via its own `config/vaulter-drive.php` / `config/vaulter-documents.php`
and throws if you resolve it without the package installed. The legacy
document-id-attached models (`document`, `version`, `folder`, `permission`, `comment`,
50→`share`) were fully excised — see [ADR-0014](/adr/0014-legacy-docvault-strangler).
:::

Vaulter route-binds `{storage}` and `{node}` against whatever you put here, so a host subclass
keeps resolving. See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy) for the tenant-aware-model pattern.

## Table names & prefix

Every table is named `{table_prefix}{canonical_entity}`. Configure a global prefix:

60→```php
'table_prefix' => env('VAULTER_TABLE_PREFIX', 'v_'), // v_drives, v_nodes, …
```

`Config::table('drives')` returns `v_drives`. Per-entity `table_names` overrides
are legacy upgrade inputs only: `Config::legacyTable()` reads them while migrations
normalize old physical names. Fresh installs ignore them. All core tables exist
regardless of feature flags; runtime routes and behavior still honor those flags.
Back up before upgrading; see [UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/axiomasoft/vaulter/blob/main/UPGRADE.md).

70→## Primary key strategy (`ids`)

The id strategy decides the column type of Vaulter primary keys and references.
**Default is `ulid`**. Keys owned by the host use the separate `ids.host_keys` setting (AD25).

```php
'ids' => [
    'default' => env('VAULTER_ID_STRATEGY', 'ulid'), // ulid | uuid7 | bigint
    'host_keys' => env('VAULTER_HOST_KEYS', 'string'), // string | bigint | uuid | ulid
    'strategies' => [
80→        'bigint' => \Vaulter\Schema\AutoIncrementIds::class,

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Console;

use Illuminate\Console\Command;
use Illuminate\Filesystem\Filesystem;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/** Scaffolds a consumer-owned ProfileProvider over the shared Vaulter schema. */
final class MakeProfileCommand extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'vaulter:make:profile
        {name : The profile id (snake/kebab), e.g. project_drive}
        {--host= : The host model FQCN this storage embeds into}
        {--no-grants : Generate a profile without per-node grants}
        {--force : Overwrite the provider if it already exists}';

    protected $description = 'Scaffold a Vaulter profile provider (zero-migration config envelope)';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly Filesystem $files,
    ) {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    public function handle(): int
    {
        /** @var string $rawName */
        $rawName = $this->argument('name');
        $id = Str::snake(Str::lower($rawName));
        $studly = Str::studly($id);

        $provider = $this->writeProvider(
            studly: $studly,
            id: $id,
            force: (bool) $this->option('force'),
        );

title: Database compatibility
description: Which databases Vaulter supports, what each engine needs, and the Postgres-specific behaviour (jsonb, bytea, advisory locks) the schema relies on.
outline: deep
---

# Database compatibility

Vaulter is **Postgres-first, portable to MySQL, and runs on SQLite**. The schema is one
10→shared `v_*` set of tables (see [Storage Panels](/guide/storage-panels)); nothing about it
is engine-locked, but a few features light up only on a real server. This page states what
each engine gives you and the handful of Postgres specifics the schema depends on.

## Canonical schema and upgrade

Fresh migrations create `v_drives`, `v_file_revisions`, `v_file_revision_blobs`
and every other core table regardless of enabled modules/features. The global
prefix is supported; per-table overrides are historical upgrade inputs only.
PostgreSQL 0.2 bigint and ULID dumps upgrade to the same schema as a fresh install,
20→including index names, partial predicates and foreign keys. Preflight refuses
unsafe soft-deleted rows, missing document revisions and own-tables deployments.
Back up and stop writes before changing code/schema. See
[the upgrade guide](https://github.com/axiomasoft/vaulter/blob/main/UPGRADE.md).

## Supported engines

| Engine | Status | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| **PostgreSQL 14+** | **Recommended.** The full test suite runs against Postgres in CI across every id strategy. | Production. Everything below works natively. |
30→| **SQLite** | Fully supported. The default test lane runs on in-memory SQLite. | Local development, tests, small single-file installs. |
| **MySQL 8+ / MariaDB** | Host-key types and upgrade DDL are tested. Full installation currently hits the MySQL 8 `sibling_active` generated-column/FK incompatibility. | Full schema compatibility is a pending release gate. |

::: tip PHP extension
Postgres needs the `pdo_pgsql` extension. It ships with most PHP distributions; on a stock
image install it (e.g. `docker-php-ext-install pdo_pgsql`) before pointing Vaulter at Postgres.
:::

## Why Postgres is the recommended lane

40→A few parts of Vaulter are a **no-op on SQLite** and only do their real work on a server —
they are exercised on Postgres in CI so they cannot regress:

- **Content-addressed blob safety.** The race-free blob commit and the destructive
  garbage-collector run their critical section under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` + `FOR UPDATE`,
  and the GC sweep runs `SERIALIZABLE` with a retry on serialization failure. On SQLite these
  collapse to the single-writer guarantee. See [Storage & Blobs](/guide/storage-and-blobs).
- **`jsonb` containment indexes.** The activity feed's `context` and the document
  version `content` are `jsonb` on Postgres with `gin (… jsonb_path_ops)` indexes for
  containment queries; other engines store plain `json`/text and skip the gin index.
50→- **Binary document state.** The Yjs CRDT snapshot (`yjs_state`) is a binary column. Vaulter
  stores it so it round-trips losslessly on every engine, including Postgres `bytea` (which
  otherwise truncates binary at the first NUL byte through a plain string bind).

None of this needs configuration — point Vaulter at Postgres and it applies automatically.

## Id strategy × engine

The primary-key strategy is configurable (see
[Configuration → id strategy](/guide/configuration)). All three work on every engine:
60→
| Strategy | Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ulid` (default) | `char(26)` | Lexicographically sortable; lines up with the Corex/Azgard morph keys. |
| `bigint` | `bigserial` / auto-increment | Classic integer keys. |
| `uuid7` | native `uuid` on Postgres | Time-ordered UUIDs; uses Postgres' native `uuid` type. |

The recursive folder tree (`v_nodes.parent_id → v_nodes.id`) is a self-referencing foreign
key. PostgreSQL and SQLite migrate it under all three strategies. MySQL 8 currently
rejects the STORED `sibling_active` column over the cascading `parent_id` foreign key
70→(error 1215); this pre-existing installation defect remains a release gate.

## Case-insensitive search

Node- and document-name search is **case-folded** (`lower(col) like lower(?)`), so a query
matches regardless of case on every engine — including Postgres, whose `like` is
case-sensitive (unlike SQLite/MySQL). No configuration needed.

## Host keys and Spatie role grants

80→Host-owned owner, subject, author, tenant and actor columns use `ids.host_keys` (AD25),

---
title: Database compatibility
description: Which databases Vaulter supports, what each engine needs, and the Postgres-specific behaviour (jsonb, bytea, advisory locks) the schema relies on.
outline: deep
---

# Database compatibility

Vaulter is **Postgres-first, portable to MySQL, and runs on SQLite**. The schema is one
shared `v_*` set of tables (see [Storage Panels](/guide/storage-panels)); nothing about it
is engine-locked, but a few features light up only on a real server. This page states what
each engine gives you and the handful of Postgres specifics the schema depends on.

## Canonical schema and upgrade

Fresh migrations create `v_drives`, `v_file_revisions`, `v_file_revision_blobs`
and every other core table regardless of enabled modules/features. The global
prefix is supported; per-table overrides are historical upgrade inputs only.
PostgreSQL 0.2 bigint and ULID dumps upgrade to the same schema as a fresh install,
including index names, partial predicates and foreign keys. Preflight refuses
unsafe soft-deleted rows, missing document revisions and own-tables deployments.
Back up and stop writes before changing code/schema. See
[the upgrade guide](https://github.com/axiomasoft/vaulter/blob/main/UPGRADE.md).

## Supported engines

| Engine | Status | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| **PostgreSQL 14+** | **Recommended.** The full test suite runs against Postgres in CI across every id strategy. | Production. Everything below works natively. |
| **SQLite** | Fully supported. The default test lane runs on in-memory SQLite. | Local development, tests, small single-file installs. |
| **MySQL 8+ / MariaDB** | Host-key types and upgrade DDL are tested. Full installation currently hits the MySQL 8 `sibling_active` generated-column/FK incompatibility. | Full schema compatibility is a pending release gate. |

::: tip PHP extension
Postgres needs the `pdo_pgsql` extension. It ships with most PHP distributions; on a stock
image install it (e.g. `docker-php-ext-install pdo_pgsql`) before pointing Vaulter at Postgres.
:::

## Why Postgres is the recommended lane

A few parts of Vaulter are a **no-op on SQLite** and only do their real work on a server —
they are exercised on Postgres in CI so they cannot regress:

- **Content-addressed blob safety.** The race-free blob commit and the destructive
  garbage-collector run their critical section under `pg_advisory_xact_lock` + `FOR UPDATE`,
  and the GC sweep runs `SERIALIZABLE` with a retry on serialization failure. On SQLite these
  collapse to the single-writer guarantee. See [Storage & Blobs](/guide/storage-and-blobs).
- **`jsonb` containment indexes.** The activity feed's `context` and the document
  version `content` are `jsonb` on Postgres with `gin (… jsonb_path_ops)` indexes for
  containment queries; other engines store plain `json`/text and skip the gin index.
- **Binary document state.** The Yjs CRDT snapshot (`yjs_state`) is a binary column. Vaulter
  stores it so it round-trips losslessly on every engine, including Postgres `bytea` (which
  otherwise truncates binary at the first NUL byte through a plain string bind).

None of this needs configuration — point Vaulter at Postgres and it applies automatically.

## Id strategy × engine

The primary-key strategy is configurable (see
[Configuration → id strategy](/guide/configuration)). All three work on every engine:

| Strategy | Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ulid` (default) | `char(26)` | Lexicographically sortable; lines up with the Corex/Azgard morph keys. |
| `bigint` | `bigserial` / auto-increment | Classic integer keys. |
| `uuid7` | native `uuid` on Postgres | Time-ordered UUIDs; uses Postgres' native `uuid` type. |

The recursive folder tree (`v_nodes.parent_id → v_nodes.id`) is a self-referencing foreign
key. PostgreSQL and SQLite migrate it under all three strategies. MySQL 8 currently
rejects the STORED `sibling_active` column over the cascading `parent_id` foreign key
(error 1215); this pre-existing installation defect remains a release gate.

## Case-insensitive search

Node- and document-name search is **case-folded** (`lower(col) like lower(?)`), so a query
matches regardless of case on every engine — including Postgres, whose `like` is
case-sensitive (unlike SQLite/MySQL). No configuration needed.

## Host keys and Spatie role grants

Host-owned owner, subject, author, tenant and actor columns use `ids.host_keys` (AD25),

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Profiles;

/** A named policy for drives sharing the configured Vaulter schema. */
final class Profile
{
    /** @param array<string, bool> $features */
    public function __construct(
        private string $id = '',
        private ?string $hostModel = null,
        private bool $hasGrants = true,
        private array $features = [],
    ) {}

    public function id(string $id): self
    {
        $this->id = $id;

        return $this;
    }

    public function host(string $model): self
    {
        $this->hostModel = $model;

        return $this;
    }

    public function grants(): self
    {
        $this->hasGrants = true;

        return $this;
    }

    public function withoutGrants(): self
    {
        $this->hasGrants = false;

        return $this;
    }

    /** @param array<string, bool> $flags */
    public function features(array $flags): self
    {
        $this->features = [...$this->features, ...$flags];

        return $this;
    }

    public function feature(string $name, bool $on = true): self
    {
        $this->features[$name] = $on;

        return $this;
    }

    public function getId(): string
    {
        return $this->id;
    }

    public function hostModel(): ?string
    {
        return $this->hostModel;
    }

    public function hasGrants(): bool
    {
        return $this->hasGrants;
    }

    public function featureEnabled(string $name): bool
    {
        if (array_key_exists($name, $this->features)) {
            return $this->features[$name];
        }

        return match ($name) {
            'grants' => $this->hasGrants,
            'versions', 'blobs', 'tags', 'activity', 'uploads', 'extra_data', 'reliability' => true,
            'share_links', 'public_listing', 'document_versions' => false,
            default => false,
        };
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Drive\Events\StorageCreated;
use Vaulter\Enums\Drive\NodeKind;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\DriveReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\DriveStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * Get-or-create a storage container for a host entity within a panel (§2.1), with
 * automatic root-folder provisioning. The polymorphic owner triple
 * (owner_type, owner_id, panel) is the idempotency key — guarded by the partial
 * UNIQUE index defineStorages adds, so concurrent first-touches converge on one
 * row (the INSERT loser catches the unique violation and re-reads).
 *
 * The storage's defaults come from the panel: disk from config storage.default_disk
 * and storage_type from the resolved Panel. A fresh storage gets a kind=folder
 * root node, and root_node_id is repointed at it once it exists (the schema leaves
 * that pair without a hard FK to dodge the chicken-and-egg insert order).
 */
final readonly class StorageManager
{
    public function __construct(
        private DriveReadRepository $read,
        private DriveStoreRepository $store,
        private NodeStoreRepository $nodes,
        private VaulterDatabase $database,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Resolve (or provision) the storage mounted on $owner within $panel.
     * Idempotent: a second call returns the same row.
     */
    public function forOwner(Model $owner, string $panel = 'default'): Drive
    {
        $existing = $this->read->forOwner(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);

        if ($existing instanceof Drive) {
            return $existing;
        }

        try {
            return $this->provision(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException) {
            // Lost the create race — the (owner_type, owner_id, panel) unique index
            // is the backbone; re-read the winner.
            $winner = $this->read->forOwner(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);

            if ($winner instanceof Drive) {
                return $winner;
            }

            throw new \RuntimeException(
                'Lost the storage provisioning race but the winning row is not visible.',
            );
        }
    }

    /**
     * Create the storage row + its root folder node in one transaction and repoint
     * root_node_id at the node.
     */
    private function provision(Model $owner, string $panel): Drive
    {
        return $this->database->transaction(function () use ($owner, $panel): Drive {
            $storage = $this->store->create([
                'profile' => $panel,
                'owner_type' => $owner->getMorphClass(),
                'owner_id' => $owner->getKey(),
                'name' => $this->defaultName($owner),
                'disk' => Config::defaultDisk(),
                'used_bytes' => 0,
            ]);

            $root = $this->nodes->create([
                'drive_id' => $storage->id,
                'parent_id' => null,
                'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
                'name' => '',
                'size_bytes' => 0,
            ]);

            $this->store->setRootNode(storage: $storage, rootNodeId: $root->id);

            event(new StorageCreated(storage: $storage->refresh(), root: $root));

            return $storage;
        });
    }

    /**
     * Resolve the root folder node of a storage, provisioning a missing one
     * (defensive — a storage created outside this manager may lack a root).
     */
    public function root(Drive $storage): Node
    {
        $root = $storage->rootNode()->first();

        if ($root instanceof Node) {
            return $root;
        }

        return $this->database->transaction(function () use ($storage): Node {
            $root = $this->nodes->create([
                'drive_id' => $storage->id,
                'parent_id' => null,
                'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
                'name' => '',
                'size_bytes' => 0,
            ]);
